name: Engine M6: 3D post-processing on three layers
description: Adds a pmndrs postprocessing chain (bloom, vignette, chromatic aberration, noise, depth of field, brightness/contrast, hue/saturation, ACES tone mapping last) to each three layer that asks for it, drawn through the shared offscreen renderer, with postfx:<id> tween targets. Verifies transparency is kept.

userStories.title: Effect table: create each postFx effect with defaults and tweenable fields
userStories.description: As an engine developer, I want one table from postFx type to effect constructor and tweenable fields so that adding an effect is one entry.
steps: Read engine/docs/05-filters-postfx.md (the effect table) and check every field name in node_modules/postprocessing/build/types/index.d.ts.

Create engine/src/three/postfx/effects.ts exporting POSTFX_DEFS: Record<PostFxType, { defaults; create(params, camera): Effect; tweenable: Record<string, { kind: 'number' | 'deg'; get(e): number; set(e, v): void }> }> for the 7 types.
Create engine/src/three/postfx/effects.test.ts constructing each effect in jsdom (if a constructor needs WebGL and fails in jsdom, test its def with vi.mock of that class and note which in notes).
acceptanceCriteria: POSTFX_DEFS.bloom.create({ intensity: 2 }, camera) gives an effect whose intensity is 2 and luminanceMaterial.threshold 0.85
Every tweenable key of every type round-trips through set and get (or, for mocked classes, writes the documented field)

userStories.title: buildPostFxChain: composer, passes, tone mapping swap, draw, dispose
userStories.description: As an engine developer, I want a chain that renders a scene through effects on the shared renderer and leaves the renderer as it found it so that layers without post-processing are not affected.
steps: Read engine/docs/05-filters-postfx.md '3D post-processing chain' (composer options, RenderPass clearing to transparent, one EffectPass with ToneMappingEffect last, NoToneMapping during draw then restore, setSize once, render(0)).
Create engine/src/three/postfx/chain.ts exporting PostFxChain and buildPostFxChain(renderer, scene, camera, specs, size) returning null when no spec is enabled.
resolveTarget(id, prop) returns a TargetRef on a proxy that calls the def's set ('deg' kind for hue).
Create engine/src/three/postfx/chain.test.ts with vi.mock('postprocessing') recording constructor calls and passes, and a fake renderer object with a toneMapping field.
acceptanceCriteria: With specs [bloom, vignette (enabled false)] the chain makes one EffectPass whose effects are [BloomEffect, ToneMappingEffect] in that order
During draw the fake renderer's toneMapping is NoToneMapping and after draw it is back to ACESFilmicToneMapping, also when composer.render throws
buildPostFxChain with only disabled specs returns null

userStories.title: Hook the chain into ThreeNode and route postfx:<id> targets
userStories.description: As an author, I want postFx on a three layer to draw and to be tweenable from the doc so that bloom can swell on the hero moment.
steps: Read engine/docs/05-filters-postfx.md 'Hooking post-processing into ThreeNode' and engine/src/three/threeNode.ts.

In engine/src/three/threeNode.ts: after the rig is built, set this.postFx = buildPostFxChain(shared.renderer, rig.scene, rig.camera, layer.postFx, { width, height }); pass draw: postFx?.draw to shared.render; route resolveTarget('postfx:<id>', prop) to postFx.resolveTarget; dispose it in destroy().
Create engine/src/three/postfx/index.ts re-exporting the chain and effect table.
acceptanceCriteria: A three layer with postFx [{ id: 'glow', type: 'bloom' }] gives resolveTarget('postfx:glow', 'intensity') non-null; 'postfx:none' gives null
update(t) passes a draw function to the fake renderer's render request when postFx is set and none when the layer has no postFx

userStories.title: Browser check: post-processing look, determinism and transparency
userStories.description: As a project owner, I want to see bloom and vignette on the can over the plate, and know whether transparency survives, before the runtime ships.
steps: Add the three-postfx fixture to the smoke page's select, and a readout of the RGBA of pixel (2, 2) of the node's own 2D canvas after each seek (shared edit).
Open http://localhost:5173/motion-three-smoke.html, pick three-postfx, seek to 1 s and 3 s, compare to the same fixture with postFx removed in a scratch copy, save screenshots to debug/engine/.

If the corner alpha is not 0 with a transparent background: add the cross-field rule to engine/src/schema/doc.ts (a three layer with enabled postFx needs an opaque background), set background in three-postfx.json, add a test for the rule, and record the finding in notes. If it is 0, record that in notes.
acceptanceCriteria: Bloom is visible on the can's highlights and the vignette darkens the corners of the layer (screenshots saved, described in notes)
Seeking to 2 s, 0, then 2 s gives the same canvas hash both times at 2 s
notes states the measured corner alpha and which branch of step 4 was taken

Verify in the browser: with the dev server on http://localhost:5173 (owner-run; else `npm run engine:e2e` once it exists), open the page named in the story, confirm the stated behaviour, save a screenshot to debug/engine/, and record what you saw in `notes`
userStories.notes: Browser check on the owner's dev server (http://localhost:5173/motion-three-smoke.html), driven with Playwright/Chromium. Shared edit to engine/lab/three-smoke.tsx: added the three-postfx fixture to the select plus a readout, after every seek, of pixel (2,2) of the node's own 2D canvas (read as (node.display as Sprite).texture.source.resource). MEASURED CORNER ALPHA = 0: pixel (2,2) is rgba(0,0,0,0) at 1 s and 3 s with the transparent background, so STEP 4 BRANCH A was taken - transparency survives the composer (RenderPass clears to alpha 0, EffectComposer alpha:true); engine/src/schema/doc.ts was NOT changed and three-postfx.json keeps background 'transparent' with postFx enabled. For m7: motion-lab.spec.ts should assert layerPixel('hero', 2, 2)[3] === 0, not the opaque-background assertion. LOOK: bloom is clearly visible as a soft halo around the can's silhouette (the scratch no-postFx copy has none); the vignette darkens drawn pixels (the can's top edge measures rgb(238,240,241) without postFx vs rgb(233,236,238) with it) but cannot darken the fully transparent layer corners, so there is no visible corner darkening. Screenshots saved to debug/engine/: three-postfx-1.0.png, three-postfx-3.0.png, three-postfx-nofx-1.0.png, three-postfx-nofx-3.0.png (the -nofx pair came from a scratch copy of the fixture with postFx: []). DETERMINISM: the page's 2.0, 0, 2.0 compare reports the same 64x36 canvas hash both times at 2.0 s (159044155503). LIMITATION (pre-existing m4 smoke-page bug, NOT postFx): seeking 1 s vs 3 s is byte-identical for three-postfx and three-primitives because buildTimeline's timeline.set({}, {}, duration) sets the timeline end to duration and the unpositioned fromTo tweens are then appended after it, so the page's own camera-dolly/object-rotation tweens never play in 0..duration; only a glTF-mixer fixture (three-gltf) visibly moves on seek. Left as-is because the m6 shared edit is limited to the fixture + corner readout. GATES: npm run typecheck pass; npm run lint pass; npx vitest run engine/src/three engine/src/schema engine/fixtures = 157/157 pass; npm test is red with 43 failing files, all pre-existing and outside engine/ (38 web/** 'React.act is not a function' under React 19, plus fixtures/s08a seed, fixtures/s09 transcripts, scripts/preflight/docs.test.ts lockfile, server/http/client-ip.test.ts).

metadata.standingRule: Engine PRD. Everything is offline and free: unit tests in vitest (jsdom project) and browser checks on the engine lab pages. The director app is not changed.
guardrails: Work offline. The only network use allowed is `npm install`. Tests never fetch; browser checks load assets from web/public.
Never commit, push, tag, publish to npm, deploy or change repository settings. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.

Read engine/docs/README.md and the spec doc the story names before writing code. The spec is the contract: if it is wrong or impossible, do the closest thing that works and explain the difference in notes.

Porting is allowed: read tmp/reacthub-pixitweenjs/src (a read-only copy of the library, inside this repo) and copy what engine/docs/port-map.md says. Never edit anything under tmp/. Every ported file starts with `// Ported from reacthub-pixitweenjs <path> (MIT).` and is cleaned up to strict TypeScript.
No `@ts-nocheck` and no `@ts-ignore` under engine/. `@ts-expect-error` only with a reason on the same line.
engine/ must not import from web/, server/, shared/, `reacthub-pixitweenjs`, `@pixi/react` or `@react-three/*`. Only the web stub files listed in metadata.sharedEdits may import engine/.

Do not touch the director app: nothing under server/, shared/, web/src/ (except the stub files under web/ listed in metadata.sharedEdits) or the existing e2e/ specs. Config files only as listed in metadata.sharedEdits.
Everything you build goes under engine/ (src/, fixtures/, lab/, e2e/, docs/). Edit only the files named in the story's steps and their tests, plus the small edits listed in metadata.sharedEdits.

Determinism: no Math.random, Date.now or performance.now in anything that affects pixels; no GSAP `overwrite`, no `immediateRender: true`, no infinite `repeat` (engine/docs/02-timeline.md, determinism rules).
jsdom has no 2D canvas context and no WebGL: unit-test pure logic and object construction; check drawing in the browser. Never weaken a test to make it pass.
Do not add a dependency the spec does not name (`postprocessing` and `@types/three` are already declared).

Debug output and screenshots go to debug/engine/ (gitignored). For a browser check use the dev server the owner runs on http://localhost:5173 (do not start another on a different port); if it is not running, run `npm run engine:e2e` instead.
Record only real results. Never invent measurements or test output.

The shared edit to engine/src/three/threeNode.ts is limited to building, routing and disposing the chain. The shared edit to engine/src/schema/doc.ts is allowed only if the transparency check fails (US-004).
